messages.subject: a non-reactive button with a resetable value
parts:
I have been using a checkbox to get my app to add regression residuals to a dataframe (see code-snippet below wich is part of a non-reactive function). It works ok but I would prefer to use button. I have been trying to use actionButton (in shiny-incubator) but I can't get it to work the way I want (or I get side-effects that are not wanted).

if(input$addoutput == TRUE) {
var.name <- "residuals"
changedata(result$residuals, var.name)
}

It would be nice if I could add a button to ui.R that, when clicked (sets) a global variable to TRUE that can reset to FALSE when an action has been completed. The snippet above would then look something like this:

if(avar == TRUE) {
var.name <- "residuals"
changedata(result$residuals, var.name)
  avar = FALSE
}

A similar button might be useful for file.choos() to load data into an app.

Full app-code is on github - https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny/tree/master/inst/dev

messages.author: ca443e6eaa0e78ed
messages.subject: Re: a non-reactive button with a resetable value
parts:
Hi Vincent,

I spent most of today looking at your code, it turned out to be extremely interesting because there is a circular dependency in there. main.regression both reads and writes the dataset.

I made a fix that puts the button-handling code in a much more sensible place, and sent you a pull request, BUT it looks like I was using a version of your code that was two commits back. I couldn't understand the last two commits with a quick look and don't have more time today to look at it. But I wanted to explain to you what is different about my commit, so you can figure out the right thing to do to your current code.

The core issue was that main.regression contained the button-handling code. That means it is handling two completely distinct tasks: calculating the regression, and responding to the button clicks. These are not only two distinct tasks, but they are also distinct in nature: the former task has no side effects, its return value is depended upon by other reactive stuff, and you can trust the reactive system to let it run whenever; the latter task is all side effect (updating the data), nothing depends on it directly, and it MUST only execute when the button is clicked.

To me that means these are screaming to be two separate entities. Calculating the regression is a reactive function, and handling the button click is an observer (using the actionButton/isolate pattern to make sure it only runs on click).

Once I extracted the button handling code and put it in its own observer, everything seemed to work.

Looks like I have it working. Thanks for your input Joe.

messages.subject: Re: a non-reactive button with a resetable value
parts: Thanks for the follow-up Winston. Joe helped me to setup datasets in my app so they can be changed and the changes shown immediately throughout the app. He suggested setting a new.env() and putting all datasets into that environment. With the new reactiveValues function that doesn't seem to be required anymore. Below a (slightly) simplified version of the code in question. The user runs a regression and then wants to append residuals to the dataset. The observe function carries this out when the user clicks a button (linked to input$saveres). The residuals get added when I use data that is in a package (e.g., the car package) or data like mtcars, rock, etc. However, with data loaded by the user (see loadUserData) it does not. This worked with reactiveValue but not with reactiveValues(). If you need more information please let me know or see https://github.com/mostly-harmless/damshiny/  (the reactiveValues branch).

main.regression <- function(state) {
formula <- paste(state$var1, "~", paste(state$var2, collapse = " + "))

lm(formula, data = getdata())
}

regression <- reactive(function() {
if(is.null(input$var2)) return("Please select one or more independent variables")
main.regression(as.list(input))
})

observe(function() {
if (input$saveres == 0) return()
isolate(
changedata(regression()$residuals, "residuals")
)
})

changedata <- function(addCol = NULL, addColName = "") {
# function that changes data as needed
if(is.null(addCol) || addColName == "") return()
  # We don't want to take a reactive dependency on anything
  isolate(
  values[[input$datasets]][[addColName]] <- addCol
  )
}

getdata <- function(dataset = input$datasets) {
  values[[dataset]]
}

loadUserData <- function(uFile) {

# filename <- uFile$name
ext <- file_ext(uFile)
objname <- robjname <- sub(paste(".",ext,sep = ""),"",basename(uFile))
ext <- tolower(ext)

if(ext == 'rda' || ext == 'rdata') {
# objname will hold the name of the object inside the R datafile
 objname <- robjname <- load(uFile)
values[[robjname]] <- get(robjname)
}

if(datasets[1] == 'choosefile') {
datasets <<- c(objname)
} else {
datasets <<- unique(c(objname,datasets))
}

if(ext == 'csv') {
values[[objname]] <- read.csv(uFile)
}
}

loadPackData <- function(pFile) {

robjname <- data(list = pFile)
values[[robjname]] <- get(robjname)
datasets <<- unique(c(robjname,datasets))

}
